messages:
sunleaf-infra: hey team — our webhook callbacks to Redwood started failing around 03:04 UTC this morning. We see 403s from your endpoint but our allowlist is up to date with the IPs you provided last week. can you confirm if your egress IPs changed?

maya: sorry you're seeing that. can you paste a quick example error from your side and the org id?

sunleaf-infra: org id sunleaf-prod. sample curl from our payload delivery log: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/webhooks/ingest -H "Authorization: Bearer ********" -d '{}'` -> `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json
{"error":"forbidden","message":"request origin not allowlisted"}`. Our firewall only allows 54.198.12.34 (what you gave last Friday).

maya: thanks. tagging neteng — @ashwin can you check if any egress rotation/maintenance hit the Portland cluster overnight?

ashwin: looking now. egress-rotation-bot: scheduled rotation rot-2026-03-16-pt1 executed for cluster portland-1 at 03:00 UTC, replaced NAT gateway addresses.

ashwin: confirmed — we rotated NATs in portland at 03:00. new egress IPs for that pool are 54.198.56.10 and 54.198.56.11 (short window rolling). the rotation should have been in our customer notice but looks like this org was not flagged for the advisory, sorry.

sunleaf-infra: ok that explains it. do you publish the new list anywhere programmatically? we can't update allowlists manually every time — it's a big ops headache.

jordan: we can confirm where we publish ranges. Jordan (customer-success): we have an egress-ip feed in the customer portal (Settings -> Network -> Egress IPs) and an S3-signed manifest URL we can add you to. i'll DM the link. also we offer static IPs via a dedicated reserved NAT for enterprise plans if pinning is required.

sunleaf-infra: DM'd the org id, thanks. can you confirm the exact IPs we should add right now so we can get traffic flowing?

ashwin: add 54.198.56.10/32 and 54.198.56.11/32 for immediate recovery. also we recommend adding the whole /24 block 54.198.56.0/24 for the short term if your firewall supports it to avoid repeated churn during rotations. Permanent solution: request a pinned egress allocation (Dedicated) or use the published manifest URL and automate allowlist updates in your firewall.

sunleaf-infra: adding them now. one quick question — are these IPv4 only? we use IPv6 allowlists too for some endpoints.

ashwin: current NATs are IPv4 only; we don't have static IPv6 egress for hosted at the moment. noted as product feedback.

maya: a couple of asks so we can close this cleanly: 1) sunleaf, please confirm once your deliveries are passing; 2) ashwin, can you add a short incident note to the cluster's rotation runbook so we don't miss customer notifies next time; 3) jordan, please share the manifest link to the support thread so sunleaf can automate.

sunleaf-infra: deliveries resumed after adding the two IPs. thanks. :thumbsup:

ashwin: done — added runbook note and flagged rotation-notifications to include any orgs with recent allowlist changes. rot job id rot-2026-03-16-pt1 -> ticket NET-7801.

jordan: manifest link DMed in thread. also created a small playbook we can share with customers for automating firewall updates (uses the manifest JSON and validates IPs before applying). i'll attach to the portal.

maya: great. marking this resolved for now but keeping the thread open for follow-ups. if you want us to provision a pinned egress for sunleaf we can start the evaluation.

sunleaf-infra: please open an evaluation ticket — we'd like a pinned NAT for prod. thanks everyone.

egress-rotation-bot: notice: next planned rotation window for portland cluster is 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC. customers with manual allowlists should consider temporary widening or request pinned egress prior to the date.
